description: In this hackathon, we are focusing on the "Abandoned but Not Forgotten: Storytelling of NASA's Abandoned Equipment on the Moon and Mars" challenge. Our goal is to bring to light the stories of the silent explorers left behind in the depths of space. By combining our technical hardware and software capabilities with emotional and immersive storytelling, we will present a unique and digitized narrative experience that will give a "voice" back to these forgotten pieces of equipment.
summary: Not Abandoned, A Legacy Left Behind” is a 7-slide story presentation that tells school-age children about the rovers NASA left on Mars and the Moon. It follows Spirit, Opportunity and the Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicles. For each machine, it explains why it was sent, why it went silent and what scientific legacy it left, in simple language based on NASA sources. The final story shows, with a simple error-checking example, how such machines could send data safely back to Earth. Our goal is to show abandoned hardware not as junk but as a legacy that still inspires, and to spark curiosity about space in young learners.
details: The project is a 7-slide story presentation that tells school-age children about the rovers NASA left on Mars and the Moon: Spirit, Opportunity and the Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicles. Each story covers why the machine was sent, how it ended and what scientific legacy it left. Children learn real space science (signs of past water on Mars, Moon exploration) through short, simple stories instead of technical text. The intended impact is to change how young people see “abandoned” space hardware: not as junk, but as a legacy that still inspires curiosity about space. The presentation was prepared as a PowerPoint file and shared through Google Slides. All facts come from NASA pages listed on the final References slide, and AI assistance was used for text writing. The creative side is the “legacy, not junk” idea, and a simple error-checking example (a check bit) that explains in child-friendly language how rover data can reach Earth without being corrupted. Our team, with a communication technology background, considered age-appropriate language, accuracy of NASA facts, a clear visual design, and the 7-slide limit.
